import { defineConfig } from "vite";import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";import tsconfigPaths from "vite-tsconfig-paths";export default defineConfig({  plugins: [react(), tsconfigPaths()],  server: {    port: 3000,  },  build: {    target: "es2022",    sourcemap: false,  },});

The clearest illustration is the runtime stage of Dockerfile:

FROM node:22-alpineRUN npm install -g serveWORKDIR /appCOPY --from=builder /app/dist ./publicEXPOSE 12445CMD ["serve", "public", "-l", "12445"]

Not even Node has to run — just a static file sitting there, the runtime stage is almost boringly clean…

A causal chain I cut along the way

The font chain spans two commits. In the Vite migration commit (3075556), Inter in next/font/google was no longer usable, so I swapped in a local @fontsource package, which suddenly added about 5MB of woff2 for Chinese fonts; ten minutes later in ae004b3 it hit me — the main reason I’d installed PWA in the first place was to cache those 5MB, so I might as well switch to a system font stack (PingFang / YaHei / Roboto), and deleted @fontsource along with the PWA.

“Deleted” isn’t quite accurate though… digging through the log, I found the PWA had already been deleted once back in 5321a54, then reinstalled later — this was the second deletion. So this wasn’t some clean decision at all; it took two rounds of back-and-forth before it settled down.

And deleting a PWA isn’t just deleting code. Old visitors still have the old Service Worker in their browsers, so I had to leave a tombstone SW to let it unregister itself:

// Tombstone service worker.self.addEventListener("install", () => self.skipWaiting());self.addEventListener("activate", (event) => {  event.waitUntil(    (async () => {      const names = await caches.keys();      await Promise.all(names.map((n) => caches.delete(n)));      await self.registration.unregister();      const clients = await self.clients.matchAll({ type: "window" });      for (const client of clients) client.navigate(client.url);    })(),  );});

Clear the cache, unregister, then have already-open pages navigate again… removing a feature is way more hassle than removing code.

The unfinished wrap-up

Then comes the not-so-glorious part. As of today:

  • README.md still says Next.js 15 + Serwist + Tailwind 3 + NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix, but it’s actually Vite 7 + Tailwind 4 + VITE_ — every technical description is wrong
  • .github/workflows/build.yml:53's artifact is path: out, while Vite output lives in dist, so whatever CI uploads has long been empty
  • The CSS path in components.json points to src/app/globals.css, but the file moved to src/globals.css ages ago
  • app-footer.tsx:38's suppressHydrationWarning is dead code — there’s no hydration at all anymore

The funniest part is that 0e83f8c, the time I took Nuxt offline, the commit body actually listed a complete “5 things you have to change along with the framework swap”: Dockerfile, vercel.json, GitHub Actions artifact path, .dockerignore, README… The checklist wasn’t wrong by a single word — the next migration just didn’t follow it, and I didn’t bother to look either.

One more: while cleaning up for e6b5d81 I found @radix-ui/react-slot and class-variance-authority, two dependencies installed by the shadcn scaffold — installed 4-21, deleted 5-14, zero imports across 23 days (there’s no button.tsx in the project at all); .vscode still recommends Vue.volar, leftovers from two frameworks ago. Adding a dependency takes a second; deleting one takes three weeks…

The one that moved in

On the other side is vns, a Galgame resource site. In the same repo you can see the full three-stage evolution: the old branch is Hexo 8.1.1 + NexT, dev/beast is Hugo Extended, and over on vns, the dev server in .claude/launch.json points straight at the neighboring vns-next directory running bun run dev — two repos migrating side by side for comparison.

There were three reasons to move it into Next.js.

First, a static site has no server, so API keys can only sit in plaintext in the frontend JS. At the time, main.js had this One API key just lying there:

const API_URL = "https://example.com/v1/chat/completions";const API_KEY = "sk-xxxx";  // 就这么明文躺着

That’s the only option for AI features on a pure static site — no choice. The same thing in Next.js can go into a Route Handler and the key stays server-side. Also, remember to rotate any key that has been in a public repo; changing the code doesn’t count…

Second, this site’s “database” is 6 JSON files under data/. Ad slots, friend links, download sources, translation groups — all fake databases read at build time. Changing one row of data meant rebuilding the whole site and re-pushing the deploy branch, and that branch is 27.9MB / 1832 files… all to change one line of JSON.

Third, to create a “dynamic feel” I’d piled up over two thousand lines of client JS. main.js was 2347 lines before splitting, stuffed with swup page transitions, lazy loading, counter animations, localStorage toggles, SSE streaming requests. Later it was split into 8 ES modules and the main file dropped to 613 lines, but the pitfalls along the way were pretty typical (these are all on the dev branch):

  • 4842e804e: after splitting into ES modules, top-level variables like VALINE_CONFIG stayed in the original file. Module top-level scope doesn’t span files, so the comment component never initialized — and it was users who reported it
  • 187ad71b4: a single try/catch wrapped all the inits, so one crash mid-way killed everything after it. Users reported “comments and TOC are both broken” — the TOC was purely collateral damage. Changed to an independent catch per [name, fn]
  • d83c2801a: main.js runs before the DOM as a render-blocking script, so getElementById returns null; swup transitions also caused the global click handler to be bound repeatedly, finally bailed out with a window._fireworkBound flag

All of these are things a component lifecycle gives you for free; hand-rolling means hitting them one by one.

One more thing that’s easy to forget: URLs have to be preserved exactly… Hexo’s abbrlink short link (crc16/dec, permalink is p/:abbrlink/) became a Hugo slug, then became work.id on the new site — /p/{id}/ survived three generations of that old link. Not even the trailing slash can change — Artalk/Valine historical comments are stored under the path /p/{id}/ with the slash, and missing one character means losing comments. To that end, vns-next had to disable the framework’s built-in trailing-slash redirect and take over itself; I posted the full comments from that tug-of-war in the post about convention files.

Finally, one intermediate state. The bbps site is also output: 'export', with next.config.ts only 12 lines, and real-time data simply bypassed with client-side polling:

useEffect(() => {  fetchStats()  const id = setInterval(fetchStats, 30000)  return () => clearInterval(id)}, [fetchStats])

Hit an external API every 30 seconds — good enough… Static shell + client polling, effortless.

A month of moving things around, and it really boiled down to one question: is there anything on this site that absolutely has to live on a server? Think it over and the answer is obvious—there’s no mystery to it. Anyway, I’m out~
entry.summary: Two migrations in opposite directions, and along the way a clear explanation of which sites need a server and which don't
entry.title: In the Same Month, I Moved My Homepage Out of Next.js and Moved a Hugo Site In

entry.content:
Turning your own videos into macOS Tahoe dynamic wallpapers is actually a rather quiet little process.

The folder path is
~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.wallpaper/aerials/videos/

Inside there are usually just one or two .mov files, like
4C108785-A7BA-422E-9C79-B0129F1D5550.mov (the kind that’s around 445MB).

The steps go like this:

  1. First go to “System Settings > Wallpaper” and download a Tahoe Aerial dynamic wallpaper so the folder has something in it.
  2. Back up the original .mov file somewhere else (very important).
  3. If your video is webm, convert it to mov with ffmpeg (visually near-lossless):
ffmpeg -i input.webm -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -preset slow -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -b:a 192k output.mov

Or the more “Apple-flavored” ProRes:

ffmpeg -i input.webm -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 3 -c:a pcm_s16le output.mov
  1. Rename the converted file to exactly the same name as the original (e.g. 4C108785-… .mov).
  2. Replace it in.
  3. Go back to wallpaper settings and pick the Aerial you replaced — you should see your video moving on the lock screen and occasionally on the desktop.

The desktop usually only plays a short segment (to save power), and it moves again when you unlock or switch spaces. The lock screen loops more fully.
If you get a black screen, check whether the exported mov plays properly in QuickTime. H.264 + AAC is the most reliable.
Take your time, no rush… if you break something, just restore the backup.
The feeling of tweaking wallpapers late at night is actually quite gentle, like giving your screen a breath of your own.

This is the wallpaper I use~
entry.summary: In macOS 26.2 (Tahoe), use ffmpeg to convert webm to mov, then replace files in the system aerials folder to create a custom video dynamic wallpaper. Includes actual paths and precautions; be careful to back up.
entry.title: How to Use Your Own Video as a Dynamic Wallpaper on macOS Tahoe (Aerial Replacement Method)

entry.content:
Podman Compose is almost fully compatible with docker-compose, and rootless is safer — for everyday development you can just use it as Docker Compose ~

Core commands (copy and paste ready)

CommandDescriptionDaily usage frequency
podman-compose up -dStart in the background★★★★★
podman-compose downStop and remove containers★★★★★
podman-compose down -vRemove volumes too (full reset)★★★★
podman-compose psCheck running status★★★★★
podman-compose logs -fWatch all logs in real time★★★★
podman-compose logs -f 服务名Follow a specific service’s logs★★★★★
podman-compose buildRebuild images★★★★
podman-compose pullPull the latest images★★★
podman-compose restartRestart all services★★★
podman-compose exec 服务名 bashEnter a container★★★★★
podman-compose run --rm 服务名 命令Run a one-off task★★★★

The ones I use most (just memorize these)

# 标准启动podman-compose up -d --build# 更新镜像后启动podman-compose pull && podman-compose up -d --build# 彻底删光重来（开发时超常用）podman-compose down -v && podman-compose up -d --build# 只重启/更新某个服务podman-compose up -d --build web# 进容器修东西podman-compose exec web bash

entry.content:
Okay~ Creating a 4GB swap file for your Debian is easy~ Let’s go step by step:

# 1. 创建 4GB 的 swap 文件（用 fallocate 更快）sudo fallocate -l 4G /swapfile# 如果 fallocate 不可用，就用 dd（比较慢）# sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/swapfile bs=1M count=4096 status=progress# 2. 设置权限（很重要！）sudo chmod 600 /swapfile# 3. 设置为 swap 格式sudo mkswap /swapfile# 4. 立即启用sudo swapon /swapfile# 5. 开机自动挂载（编辑 /etc/fstab）echo '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab# 6. 检查一下～swapon --showfree -h

All done~ You should have 4GB of swap now~ Want me to help you check how it’s working? ♡
entry.summary: How to create and use a swap file on a Linux system

entry.content:
Recently, while hand-building some curious “小” website, I noticed that the ReadingTime method built into the Hugo generator — which returns the estimated reading time for a given page — isn’t very accurate for CJK languages. So I used the Plain method to get the rendered content of a given page, stripped out all the HTML tags, then used the strings.RuneCount function to get the character count of the given string, and divided that by 60 and 2 to get the reading time in minutes — in other words, reading two characters per second.

{{ div (div (.Plain | htmlUnescape | strings.RuneCount) 2) 60 }}
  • ReadingTime
  • Plain
  • strings.RuneCount
  • math.Div
entry.summary: Using the Plain method and strings.RuneCount function to calculate reading time for CJK languages

Recently, while using the Hugo framework—without a ready-made theme—to hand-build some curious “小” website, I found that when using the busuanzi counter together with the swup page transition library to switch pages, the counter data sometimes fails to display. After sending the code in the busuanzi busuanzi.pure.mini.js to an AI for analysis, I discovered that the data can be refreshed by manually calling bszCaller.fetch(). So here I’ll note down how to manually reload the busuanzi counter.

bszCaller.fetch(  "//busuanzi.ibruce.info/busuanzi?jsonpCallback=BusuanziCallback",  function (a) {    bszTag.texts(a);    bszTag.shows();  });

entry.content:
Reflector is a Python script; it fetches the latest mirror list from the Arch Linux Mirror Status page, filters out the newest mirrors and sorts them by speed, then writes the results to the /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist file.

Here I’ve documented my commonly used commands and configuration files for reflector.

Commands

reflector --country China --latest 5 --sort rate --save /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist

Configuration

--save /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist--country China--latest 5--sort rate

Filter out the 5 newest mirrors located in China and sort them by speed, then write the results to the /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist file.
entry.summary: Use Reflector to automatically update the Arch Linux mirror list, filter the 5 newest and fastest mirrors in the China region, and save them to the /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist file to improve package download efficiency.
entry.title: Common Commands and Configuration Files for Updating the Reflector Mirror List

rsync is an open-source tool for fast incremental file transfer.

Lately I’ve been transferring files frequently while using Linux, so I use rsync to meet my needs…

Here I’ll record the commands I commonly use with rsync.

rsync -ravzP ~/test i@i.cc:/home/i/

Sync the local test folder to the remote machine

rsync -ravzP i@i.cc:/home/i/test ~/

Sync the remote test folder to the local machine

entry.content:
It’s been a thousand days since I first started Genshin Impact, and I’ve finally managed to comfortably grind out full stars in the Spiral Abyss! It’s been a long time since I first got full stars…

I remember the first time I got full stars, I think I used the character-swapping method—
that is, clear floors 1 and 2 with a good team, then quit out,
swap characters for floors 2 and 3, grind through floors 1 and 2 with a relatively weaker team, and then retry floors 2 and 3.

Back to this full-star run,

on the final floor 12, that lava monster was pure torture!

To leave a full minute and a half for the second half, I restarted there several times.

That thing kept burrowing around, so I always whiffed my bursts—absolute misery.

Every attempt I’d miss full stars by just a few seconds, which put me in a foul mood, and my performance got worse each time.

It might also be because I play pretty casually, so I don’t have much skill.

Midway through the Abyss I got so mad I cursed out loud: “Damn you, miHoYo number-crunching actuaries!”

After a long stretch of painful fighting, I finally left over a minute for the second half.

And when I fought the water monster at the end, I managed to hit full stars with just seconds to spare before the seven-minute mark.

I have to say, Raiden’s buff really is satisfying! It’s just that I pulled her recently and haven’t built her much, so her potential isn’t fully realized.

Having played Genshin for so long, it’s about time I started thinking about quitting or going casual.

Because this game takes up too much time and is too grindy—so much that it’s affecting my daily life.

Taking a break for a while doesn’t work either; you lose a huge amount of resources for when you come back, and playing feels like more effort than it’s worth.

Same with artifacts—the drop rates are so deliberately low that miHoYo’s number-crunching actuaries clearly have their hands in it.

The more I think about it, the more pointless it feels, and the same thought keeps popping into my head: “Am I playing the game, or is the game playing me?”

After all, miHoYo itself said: play if you like it, and don’t force yourself if you don’t—it’s a two-way choice.

So maybe in the near future… the red thread connecting me and this game for a thousand days will be cut.

When I pick up new games in the future, I’ll probably think a bit more carefully—

at least about whether it’s actually a game, and not some organization’s experiment using the public as lab rats.
entry.summary: From starting Genshin Impact until now, it has been a thousand days, and I can finally smoothly grind out full stars in the Abyss! It has been a long time since I first got full stars..
entry.title: After a Thousand Days of Genshin Impact, Finally Reached Full Stars in the Abyss

Having freeloaded without a legit copy for quite a while, I saw the ridiculously slashed price this time, and the urge to finally pay up and go legit Minecraft suddenly hit me…

0x0001

Deluxe edition 59.50, standard edition 44.50 — the prices are absolutely slashed to the bone. If not now, when?!

Buying from the official Minecraft website ran into country and region restrictions,

Open the config file _config.next.yml of the NexT theme, and uncomment head to enable the custom file configuration option

# Define custom file paths.# Create your custom files in site directory `source/_data` and uncomment needed files below.custom_file_path:  #head: source/_data/head.njk  #header: source/_data/header.njk  #sidebar: source/_data/sidebar.njk  #postMeta: source/_data/post-meta.njk  #postBodyStart: source/_data/post-body-start.njk  #postBodyEnd: source/_data/post-body-end.njk  #footer: source/_data/footer.njk  #bodyEnd: source/_data/body-end.njk  #variable: source/_data/variables.styl  #mixin: source/_data/mixins.styl  #style: source/_data/styles.styl  head: source/_data/head.njk

Create a new file siteroot/source/_data/head.njk

Open the siteroot/source/_data/head.njk file and paste the following code into it

<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://registry.npmmirror.com/weblive2d/latest/files/waifu.css"><script async src="https://registry.npmmirror.com/weblive2d/latest/files/js/autoload.js"></script>

entry.content:
Preface

Let me write down my second-ever experience with a lucid dream and dream control that I had a while back…

As for the first lucid dream, it happened many years ago. From what I vaguely remember, I didn’t succeed at dream control that time, and I’ve mostly forgotten the details anyway, so I’ll let it go and not dwell on it. No record for that one…

Before Sleep

I ** jerked off** once while showering. After I got out, I watched some long videos about a passenger plane crashing after a mid-air disaster and getting ripped off buying a knockoff phone for a while, then went to sleep…

Posture

My right side was lying on the 丛雨 dakimakura of 1.8m…

Mindset

Years in advance, I had laid down a mental imprint of wanting to spend my life with a certain someone who is close to my ideal girl in my mind…

The Process

I don’t remember her face or exactly what she looked like, but I have a rough impression of the clothes she was wearing,

and during the process of disconnecting from the dream world, the brain’s cleanup mechanism caused me to lose that part of the memory…

But I clearly remember that while in the dream, I knew what clothes she was wearing…

I remember that during the dream I also successfully controlled one action in the dream,

That’s right, dream control!

I remember trying several times to issue commands of control to myself in the dream,

and after trying for a while, I finally forcibly intervened and made my dream self hug her,

and I also vaguely remember that she was a flat chest (small breasts)!

That real feeling of bodily contact, which modern technology can’t compare to, was just so awesome!

According to what I still remember, after the hug ended, she took my hand and floated up out of thin air,

and then, with the front of my belly facing the ground, we started spinning in a circular motion, slowly accelerating. The feeling of weightlessness and acceleration grew stronger and stronger,

and as we spun, the connection gradually broke, and eventually I exited the dream world…

After Waking

For a short while after waking up, I felt an unprecedented excitement, the kind of feeling you get when you’re going through a major life event,

and once I realized I was awake, I sat on the bed and thought for a little while…

It occurred to me that if I didn’t write this down in my notes, then after some time this precious experience would probably be lost forever…

By then I’d really have missed out! At that thought, I picked up the phone I’d left by the bed, opened my notes app, and started temporarily recording the specific details…

After a while, I organized the memories my brain had at the time, cross-validated each detail in the dream, and proofread the notes I’d jotted down temporarily,

and that’s how this article came to be published…

Because this sleep was very short—I woke up in less than an hour—I didn’t experience much stuff in the dream, which is a real shame…
entry.summary: Recording the process of my second experience with controlling a lucid dream in my life some time ago..
entry.title: A Record of My Second Lucid Dream Control Experience

After a long time, I’ve finally collected 9,999 Crystalflies in Genshin Impact! That’s the per-item storage cap for a full inventory—pretty neat, huh…

As a casual player who’s long since run out of things to do in this game, at some point I had a thought: “Collect Crystalflies until I hit the inventory cap.”

I don’t clear every spot each time—I just farm a few fixed locations, like: 风起地、晨曦酒庄、孤云阁、层岩巨渊 etc…

One run nets me around 40-something, and after subtracting daily expenses that leaves 30-something… Then I repeat this every day, and over time I slowly crept toward the cap.

Haha, assuming I use 5 a day, I won’t have to worry about running out of Crystalflies for the next 2,000-plus days. Awesome!

Why I Bought It

Hahaha! The crappy DRAM-less, non-in-house-NAND SSD “威刚 XPG S11 Lite 1T” that had been tormenting me for over half a year is finally replaced! I’d originally planned to wait for 铠侠 RC20 2T during JD’s Double 11 this year, when it would drop to its all-time low for the second time and then buy it. Unfortunately, SSD prices haven’t come back down yet. If I’d known, I would’ve just bought it during 618 this year and wouldn’t be losing 80+ yuan now… Plus the old SSD couldn’t hold on, and it actually gave out first… Recently, drive dropouts, blue screens, crashes, and data loss have been happening frequently, which greatly affected my daily use and was really frustrating. So when the price was still 80+ yuan above the all-time low, I finally couldn’t resist and bought 铠侠 RC20 2T! And that’s how this article came about. Needless to say, the past half year of use before the replacement was miserable—0E throwing errors and losing data every day was a real pain…

The Old Drive

Over three thousand 0E is truly outrageous… even fiercer than Samsung!

It comes with a built-in heatsink shroud, single-sided chip design, and the overall looks are decent—but looks are all it has. Because of the single-sided design, it’s a bit thinner than those with chips on both sides…

Unboxing the New Drive

JD offers 30-day price protection and 7-day no-reason returns, and I stacked a few coupons on top—not bad, though the price… well, you know how it is.

The outer packaging is standard, nothing flashy.

Because it’s single-sided, it’s fairly thin, which is nice—if you’re not worried about heat, you can even add a copper heatsink and install it in a laptop…

I have way too much software and study material data, and I couldn’t be bothered to reinstall the system, so I just used DiskGenius to migrate the data from the old SSD, then did an over-the-top install of the system to fill in the missing files. Woohoo~

Basic Specs

It’s been a while since I bought the new SSD from JD. After all, it’s an entry-level drive with in-house TLC NAND, a Pcie3.0 mid-speed SSD, and the overall experience is fine—at least it has a cache. Due to the “1,000 on the drive = 1,024 in the system” issue, the actual capacity is a bit less than the rated capacity. I bought the 2TB version, and it actually shows 1.81TB.

SSD Testing

Overall it’s fine. I’ll see after using it for a while whether it 0E. That said, RC20 failures seem pretty rare—most failures are caused by the user’s own doing… MB/s 每秒传输速度 is standard, iops 每秒读写次数 is okay, and the file benchmark 100GB performs fine, matching mid-speed Pcie3.0. After all, I don’t have a need to copy large files 24/7; stability is my top priority. Game loading generally depends on 4K随机读写 fragmented files and doesn’t care much about an SSD’s peak speed. Under normal circumstances, the gap between entry-level and top-tier SSDs is less than 2s, so personally I don’t think it’s necessary to spend more money on Pcie4.0. Stability, no data loss, and no 0E errors come first. After all, Kioxia’s predecessor is Toshiba, so stability and compatibility are pretty good… Why not buy a bulk-shipped MLC drive whose endurance crushes TLC? Heh, it’s been hammered by enterprises for so long—even if the NAND isn’t dead, the controller is on its last legs, and bulk-shipped goods have no official warranty. Of course, I can’t speak for anyone’s preferences or tastes, so forget it—I’m going for stability, hehe~~

Reposting Official Images
entry.summary: Since the old SSD has reached the end of its life, I bought a new SSD, the 'Kioxia RC20,' to keep my computer running strong!
entry.title: Double 11 Impulse Purchase: Kioxia RC20 SSD Experience

entry.content:
Exporting Comment Data

Method 1

You can go to the 管理面板 of the comments in Twikoo, select the 导出 tab, and click the 导出评论 button to export Twikoo’s comment data into a json file.

Method 2 (Recommended)

Export the comment data of Twikoo into a json file. For details, see the following article:

Twikoo 评论数据导出教程 - iMaeGoo’s Blog

Restoring Comment Data

If you only want to back up the data and have no other needs, you’re done at this step. To restore comment data later, simply select the 导入 tab, choose the source system Twikoo（JSON）, select the backup file you exported, and click 开始导入. If you also need to modify the comment data, keep reading.

Editing Comment Data

You can open the Twikoo comment data file with the .json extension using Visual Studio Code or another IDE to edit the comment data you see. You can refer to the table below for the meaning of common fields when making changes:

ValueMeaning
nickNickname
mailEmail
mailMd5Email MD5 value
linkWebsite link
uaDevice user agent code
ipIP address
masterWhether the commenter is the site owner
urlRelative path from the homepage
hrefAbsolute path of the current location when the comment was sent
commentComment content
isSpamWhether it is spam
createdCreation timestamp
updatedUpdate timestamp
avatarAvatar link
topWhether it is pinned

After editing, go to the database of your Twikoo comments—for example, my MongoDB Cloud—and delete the comment item.

Of course, you can use a better method as long as the comment item is eventually deleted…

Once you’ve finished deleting, follow the above Restoring Comment Data steps and the modification is complete.

entry.content:
Reproducing the Problem

Reproducing this problem is easy. It’s most likely a network issue: just turn off your proxy tool, accelerator, or similar network-optimization software, then make sure the pushing device’s network is within mainland China, and chances are you’ll reproduce it…

Solving the Problem

These problems are usually caused by an unstable network environment, so start with the network. First, use a network proxy tool to relay the current device’s network environment—relay the resources Hexo pushes to another device, and send them to GitHub from that device.

0x0001

I personally use Clash as the proxy medium; check the proxy port.

Note down this port 7890. If you’re using v2ray proxy, the default port is usually 1080.

0x0002

Use the following command in the terminal to change git's global proxy settings

git config --global http.proxy http://127.0.0.1:7890

--global means global, 127.0.0.1 means the local machine, and 7890 refers to the proxy port you noted down earlier.

0x0003

Change the push address to an https address. You can go to your GitHub repository, click “Code>HTTPS” and copy it.

Then edit the _config.yml configuration file in your Hexo site’s root directory to change the push address.

If you were already using an https address rather than ssh, you can skip this step.

0x0004

Then it’s the Hexo trio! Check whether the push succeeded.

hexo cl && hexo g && hexo d

Don’t forget to enable your proxy tool.
entry.summary: Resolving the spawn failed error that occurs when using the hexo d command to push with Hexo
entry.title: Resolving the spawn failed error when pushing with Hexo

For the plugin installation guide, please refer to this article by 店长: Swiper Bar

Before making any beautification tweaks, make sure your blog is running on the Hexo framework with the Butterfly theme; other frameworks or themes may not work.

Adding the Style Code

Add the following style code to your custom CSS file:

/* 文章置顶滚动栏(店长) */.blog-slider {  height: 260px !important;}.blog-slider__img {  width: 40% !important;  height: 100% !important;}@media screen and (max-width: 600px) {  .blog-slider {    padding: 0 !important;  }  .blog-slider__img {    width: 100% !important;    height: 40% !important;    padding-left: 0 !important;    padding-right: 0 !important;  }}

What this code does is change the post cover images on desktop from squares into rectangles, while on mobile they now fill the full width from edge to edge, which looks much easier on the eye.

You can keep adding your own styles either to the existing elements above, or by pressing F12 and using 开发者工具 to locate the ID of the corresponding element.

Most monitors require you to press buttons on the back to adjust brightness, and since it’s easy to forget which button controls brightness, you often end up hitting the wrong one—such a hassle!

So I went to the world’s largest sex community platform and found this Monitorian brightness-adjustment utility to replace the buttons. It makes adjusting brightness much more convenient, and the interface is somewhat similar to laptop brightness controls.

Microsoft Store 版本 offers more settings and features, such as hotkey support.

Requirements

  • Windows 7 or later
  • .NET Framework 4.8 runtime
  • DDC/CI must be enabled on the monitor; it’s usually enabled by default on modern displays

Credits

entry.content:
Background

When I first saw the buttons in the announcement bar of the Butterfly theme’s official documentation, I didn’t think much of it. But once I had a use for them, I kept wanting to add buttons to my own blog’s announcement bar. I searched the theme’s official docs from top to bottom, but they never explained how to do it. Once I realized this wasn’t a built-in feature of the theme, I planned to search for ready-made mods that others had shared, but I never could find any — maybe I just wasn’t looking hard enough (. So I wrote one myself, modeled on the style in the official docs. It uses only HTML and CSS, so it’s pretty simple.

Tutorial

0x0001

Open the Buitterfly theme config file _config.butterfly.yml, and add the following HTML code to the card_announcement: option under aside (the sidebar). Pick the snippet with however many buttons you need.

1 button

<div class="social-button"><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第一个按钮，填自己的内容</a></div>

2 buttons

<div class="social-button"><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第一个按钮，填自己的内容</a><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第二个按钮，填自己的内容</a></div>

3 buttons

<div class="social-button"><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第一个按钮，填自己的内容</a><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第二个按钮，填自己的内容</a><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第三个按钮，填自己的内容</a></div>

4 buttons

<div class="social-button"><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第一个按钮，填自己的内容</a><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第二个按钮，填自己的内容</a><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第三个按钮，填自己的内容</a><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第四个按钮，填自己的内容</a></div>

5 buttons

<div class="social-button"><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第一个按钮，填自己的内容</a><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第二个按钮，填自己的内容</a><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第三个按钮，填自己的内容</a><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第四个按钮，填自己的内容</a><a class="button--animated" href="https://baidu.com/" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">第五个按钮，填自己的内容</a></div>

If you need more buttons, just add more a tags.

0x0002

Replace the links in the href="https://baidu.com/" attribute and the text inside the a tags with your own, using my aside sidebar config as a reference.

# aside (側邊欄)# --------------------------------------aside:  enable: true  hide: false  button: true  mobile: true # display on mobile  position: right # left or right  display:    archive: true    tag: true    category: true  card_announcement:    enable: true    content: 这是一段公告内容。<div class="social-button"><a class="button--animated" href="//qm.qq.com/cgi-bin/qm/qr?_wv=1027&k=aNthm0SgxBnx28iW06K8NQmuT9OYBweY&authKey=6PPWxZgCuCAQ6L7%2BVAAjSK8c%2FMGBUbQEOyliEmhB9njVrJUoOyIaNrta2q992Ok7&noverify=0&group_code=875766458" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">👉 QQ 交流群 👈</a><a class="button--animated" href="//t.me/FullDiveSAO" rel="external nofollow noreferrer" target="_blank">👉 TG 交流群 👈</a></div>

0x0003

Add the following style code to your own custom CSS file.

/* aside公告栏按钮美化 */.social-button .button--animated {  background: #3eb8be;  color: rgb(255, 255, 255);  display: block;  margin: 4px 0;  text-align: center;  line-height: 2.4;  transition: 0.3s;  border-radius: 8px;}.social-button .button--animated:hover {  background-color: #40c4ae;}.social-button .button--animated:active {  background-color: #339ea3;}

0x0004

Finally, run the three Hexo commands and check out the result!

hexo cl; hexo g; hexo s

entry.summary: HTTP Content-type Comparison Table
entry.title: HTTP Content-type Comparison Table

entry.content:
Status CodeMeaning
100The client should continue sending the request. This interim response is used to inform the client that part of its request has been received by the server and has not yet been rejected. The client should continue sending the remainder of the request, or, if the request has already been completed, ignore this response. The server must send a final response to the client after the request is completed.
101The server has understood the client’s request and will notify the client through the Upgrade message header to use a different protocol to complete this request. After sending the final blank line of this response, the server will switch to the protocols defined in the Upgrade header. Similar measures should be taken only when switching to a new protocol is beneficial. For example, switching to a new HTTP version is more advantageous than the old version, or switching to a real-time and synchronous protocol to transmit resources that use such features.
102A status code extended by WebDAV (RFC 2518), indicating that processing will continue.
200The request has succeeded, and the response header or data body desired by the request will be returned with this response.
201The request has been fulfilled, and a new resource has been created as needed by the request, and its URI has been returned with the Location header. If the required resource cannot be created in time, ‘202 Accepted’ should be returned.
202The server has accepted the request but has not yet processed it. Just as it may be rejected, the request may or may not be executed eventually. In the case of asynchronous operations, there is no more convenient way than sending this status code. The purpose of returning a 202 status code response is to allow the server to accept requests for other processes (for example, a batch-based operation that is executed only once a day) without making the client keep the connection to the server until the batch operation is fully completed. A response that accepts the request for processing and returns 202 should include in the returned entity some information indicating the current processing status, as well as a pointer to a processing status monitor or status prediction, so that the user can estimate whether the operation has been completed.
203The server has successfully processed the request, but the entity header metainformation returned is not a definitive set valid on the origin server, but comes from a local or third-party copy. The current information may be a subset or superset of the original version. For example, including resource metadata may cause the origin server to know a superset of the metainformation. Using this status code is not required, and it is only appropriate when the response would otherwise return 200 OK.
204The server successfully processed the request but does not need to return any entity content, and wishes to return updated metainformation. The response may return new or updated metainformation in the form of entity headers. If such header information exists, it should correspond to the requested variables. If the client is a browser, the user’s browser should retain the page that sent the request without making any changes to the document view, even if, according to the specification, the new or updated metainformation should be applied to the document in the user’s browser active view. Because a 204 response is prohibited from containing any message body, it always ends with the first blank line after the message headers.
205The server successfully processed the request and did not return any content. However, unlike a 204 response, a response returning this status code requires the requester to reset the document view. This response is mainly used to immediately reset a form after accepting user input so that the user can easily start another input. Like a 204 response, this response is also prohibited from containing any message body and ends with the first blank line after the message headers.
206The server has successfully processed a partial GET request. HTTP download tools such as FlashGet or Thunder use this type of response to implement resumable downloads or to split a large document into multiple download segments for simultaneous download.
The request must contain a Range header to indicate the range of content the client wishes to obtain, and may contain If-Range as a request condition.
The response must contain the following header fields:
Content-Range to indicate the range of content returned in this response; if it is a multipart download with Content-Type multipart/byteranges, each multipart segment should contain a Content-Range field to indicate the content range of that segment. If the response contains Content-Length, its value must match the actual number of bytes of the returned content range. Date, ETag, and/or Content-Location, if the same request should have returned a 200 response. Expires, Cache-Control, and/or Vary, if their values may differ from those of other responses to the same variables. If this response request uses If-Range strong cache validation, then this response should not contain other entity headers; if this response request uses If-Range weak cache validation, then this response is prohibited from containing other entity headers; this avoids inconsistency between the cached entity content and the updated entity header information. Otherwise, this response should contain all entity header fields that should have been returned in a 200 response. If the ETag or Last-Modified header cannot match exactly, the client cache is prohibited from combining the content returned by the 206 response with any previously cached content. Any cache that does not support Range and Content-Range headers is prohibited from caching the content returned by a 206 response.
207A status code extended by WebDAV (RFC 2518), indicating that the following message body will be an XML message and may contain a series of independent response codes depending on the number of previous subrequests.
300The requested resource has a series of selectable feedback information, each with its own specific address and browser-driven negotiation information. The user or browser can choose a preferred address for redirection. Unless this is a HEAD request, the response should include an entity with a list of resource characteristics and addresses so that the user or browser can select the most suitable redirect address. The format of this entity is determined by the format defined by Content-Type. The browser may automatically make the most appropriate choice based on the response format and its own capabilities. Of course, the RFC 2616 specification does not specify how such automatic selection should be performed. If the server itself already has a preferred feedback choice, the URI of this feedback should be indicated in Location; the browser may use this Location value as the address for automatic redirection. In addition, unless otherwise specified, this response is also cacheable.
301The requested resource has been permanently moved to a new location, and any future references to this resource should use one of the URIs returned by this response. If possible, a client with link-editing capabilities should automatically change the requested address to the address returned by the server. Unless otherwise specified, this response is also cacheable. The new permanent URI should be returned in the Location field of the response. Unless this is a HEAD request, the response entity should contain a hyperlink to the new URI and a brief description. If this is not a GET or HEAD request, the browser is prohibited from automatically performing redirection unless the user confirms it, because the conditions of the request may change as a result. Note: For some browsers using HTTP/1.0, if their POST request receives a 301 response, the subsequent redirect request will become a GET request.
302The requested resource is currently responding to requests from a different URI. Because such a redirect is temporary, the client should continue to send future requests to the original address. This response is cacheable only if specified in Cache-Control or Expires. The new temporary URI should be returned in the Location field of the response. Unless this is a HEAD request, the response entity should contain a hyperlink to the new URI and a brief description. If this is not a GET or HEAD request, the browser is prohibited from automatically performing redirection unless the user confirms it, because the conditions of the request may change as a result. Note: Although RFC 1945 and RFC 2068 do not allow clients to change the request method during redirection, many existing browsers treat a 302 response as a 303 response and use GET to access the URI specified in Location, ignoring the original request method. Status codes 303 and 307 were added to clarify what kind of reaction the server expects from the client.
303The response corresponding to the current request can be found at another URI, and the client should use GET to access that resource. This method exists mainly to allow the output of a POST request activated by a script to be redirected to a new resource. This new URI is not a substitute reference for the original resource. At the same time, a 303 response is prohibited from being cached. Of course, the second request (the redirect) may be cached. The new URI should be returned in the Location field of the response. Unless this is a HEAD request, the response entity should contain a hyperlink to the new URI and a brief description. Note: Many browsers before HTTP/1.1 cannot correctly understand the 303 status. If interaction with these browsers needs to be considered, the 302 status code should be sufficient, because most browsers handle 302 responses in exactly the way the above specification requires clients to handle 303 responses.
304If the client sent a conditional GET request and the request has been allowed, and the content of the document (since the last access or according to the request conditions) has not changed, the server should return this status code. A 304 response is prohibited from containing a message body, so it always ends with the first blank line after the message headers.
The response must contain the following header information:
Date, unless the server has no clock. If a server without a clock also follows these rules, then proxy servers and clients can add the Date field to the received response headers themselves (as specified in RFC 2068), and the caching mechanism will work normally.
ETag and/or Content-Location, if the same request should have returned a 200 response.
Expires, Cache-Control, and/or Vary, if their values may differ from those of other responses to the same variables.
If this response request uses strong cache validation, then this response should not contain other entity headers; otherwise (for example, a conditional GET request uses weak cache validation), this response is prohibited from containing other entity headers; this avoids inconsistency between the cached entity content and the updated entity header information.
If a 304 response indicates that a current entity is not cached, the cache system must ignore this response and repeatedly send a request without restrictions.
If a 304 response requiring an update to a cache entry is received, the cache system must update the entire entry to reflect the values of all fields updated in the response.
305The requested resource must be accessed through the specified proxy. The Location field will give the URI information of the specified proxy, and the recipient needs to send a separate request again to access the corresponding resource through this proxy. Only the origin server can create a 305 response. Note: RFC 2068 does not clarify that a 305 response is for redirecting a single request and can only be created by the origin server. Ignoring these restrictions may lead to serious security consequences.
306In the latest version of the specification, the 306 status code is no longer used.
307The requested resource is currently responding to requests from a different URI. Because such a redirect is temporary, the client should continue to send future requests to the original address. This response is cacheable only if specified in Cache-Control or Expires. The new temporary URI should be returned in the Location field of the response. Unless this is a HEAD request, the response entity should contain a hyperlink to the new URI and a brief description. Because some browsers cannot recognize 307 responses, the above necessary information needs to be added so that users can understand and send access requests to the new URI. If this is not a GET or HEAD request, the browser is prohibited from automatically performing redirection unless the user confirms it, because the conditions of the request may change as a result.
4001. The semantics are incorrect, and the current request cannot be understood by the server. Unless modified, the client should not resubmit this request. 2. The request parameters are incorrect.
401The current request requires user authentication. This response must contain a WWW-Authenticate information header suitable for the requested resource to ask for user information. The client may resubmit a request containing the appropriate Authorization header information. If the current request already contains Authorization credentials, then the 401 response means that server authentication has rejected those credentials. If the 401 response contains the same authentication challenge as the previous response, and the browser has already attempted authentication at least once, the browser should display the entity information contained in the response to the user, because this entity information may contain relevant diagnostic information. See RFC 2617.
402This status code is reserved for possible future needs.
403The server has understood the request but refuses to execute it. Unlike a 401 response, authentication cannot help, and this request should not be resubmitted. If this is not a HEAD request and the server wishes to explain clearly why the request cannot be executed, it should describe the reason for refusal in the entity. Of course, the server may also return a 404 response if it does not want the client to obtain any information.
404The request failed, and the resource desired by the request was not found on the server. No information can tell the user whether this situation is temporary or permanent. If the server knows the situation, it should use the 410 status code to inform that the old resource has become permanently unavailable due to some internal configuration mechanism problem, and that there is no address to jump to. The 404 status code is widely used when the server does not want to reveal why the request was rejected or when no other suitable response is available.
405The request method specified in the request line cannot be used for the requested resource. This response must return an Allow header to indicate the list of request methods that the current resource can accept. Given that PUT and DELETE methods perform write operations on server resources, most web servers do not support or do not allow the above request methods under the default configuration, and will return a 405 error for such requests.
406The content characteristics of the requested resource cannot satisfy the conditions in the request headers, so a response entity cannot be generated. Unless this is a HEAD request, the response should return an entity containing a list of entity characteristics and addresses from which the user or browser can select the most suitable one. The format of the entity is determined by the media type defined in the Content-Type header. The browser can make the best choice on its own based on the format and its own capabilities. However, the specification does not define any standard for making such automatic selection.
407Similar to a 401 response, except that the client must authenticate on the proxy server. The proxy server must return a Proxy-Authenticate to perform the authentication challenge. The client can return Proxy-Authorization header information for verification. See RFC 2617.
408Request timeout. The client did not complete sending a request within the time the server was prepared to wait. The client can resubmit this request at any time without any changes.
409The request cannot be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the requested resource. This code may only be used in situations where the user is considered able to resolve the conflict and will resubmit a new request. The response should contain enough information for the user to discover the source of the conflict. Conflicts usually occur when processing PUT requests. For example, in an environment using version checking, if the version information attached to a PUT request to modify a specific resource conflicts with a previous (third-party) request, then the server should return a 409 error to inform the user that the request cannot be completed. At this time, the response entity is likely to contain a comparison of the differences between the two conflicting versions so that the user can resubmit a new merged version.
410The requested resource is no longer available on the server, and there is no known forwarding address. Such a situation should be considered permanent. If possible, a client with link-editing capabilities should delete all references to this address after obtaining user permission. If the server does not know or cannot determine whether this situation is permanent, it should use the 404 status code. Unless otherwise specified, this response is cacheable. The purpose of the 410 response is mainly to help website administrators maintain the website, notify users that the resource is no longer available, and that the server owner hopes that all remote links pointing to this resource will also be deleted. Such events are common in limited-time, value-added services. Likewise, the 410 response is also used to notify the client that on the current server site, a resource that originally belonged to an individual is no longer available. Of course, whether all permanently unavailable resources need to be marked as ‘410 Gone’, and how long this mark needs to be kept, depends entirely on the server owner.
411The server refuses to accept the request without a defined Content-Length header. After adding a valid Content-Length header indicating the length of the request message body, the client can submit the request again.
412The server failed to satisfy one or more of the preconditions given in the request header fields during verification. This status code allows the client to set preconditions in the request metainformation (request header field data) when obtaining a resource, thereby preventing the request method from being applied to resources other than the desired content.
413The server refuses to process the current request because the size of the entity data submitted by the request exceeds the range the server is willing or able to process. In this case, the server may close the connection to prevent the client from continuing to send this request. If this situation is temporary, the server should return a Retry-After response header to inform the client how long to wait before retrying.
414The length of the requested URI exceeds the length the server can interpret, so the server refuses to service the request. This is relatively rare. Common cases include: a form submission that should have used POST becomes a GET method, causing the query string to be too long. Redirect URI ‘black holes’, for example, each redirect includes the old URI as part of the new URI, causing the URI to become too long after several redirects. The client is attempting to exploit a security vulnerability in some servers to attack the server. Such servers use fixed-length buffers to read or operate on the requested URI. When the parameters after GET exceed a certain value, a buffer overflow may occur, causing arbitrary code execution[1]. Servers without such vulnerabilities should return the 414 status code.
415For the method of the current request and the requested resource, the entity submitted in the request is not in a format supported by the server, so the request is rejected.
416If the request contains a Range request header, and any data range specified in Range does not overlap with the available range of the current resource, and the request does not define an If-Range request header, then the server should return the 416 status code. If Range uses byte ranges, then this situation means that the first byte position of all data ranges specified in the request exceeds the length of the current resource. The server should also include a Content-Range entity header when returning the 416 status code to indicate the length of the current resource. This response is also prohibited from using multipart/byteranges as its Content-Type.
417The expectation specified in the Expect request header cannot be satisfied by the server, or the server is a proxy server and has clear evidence that the content of Expect cannot be satisfied at the next node on the current route.
421The number of connections from the IP address where the current client is located to the server exceeds the maximum range permitted by the server. Usually, the IP address here refers to the client address seen from the server (such as the user’s gateway or proxy server address). In this case, the calculation of the number of connections may involve more than one end user.
422The number of connections from the IP address where the current client is located to the server exceeds the maximum range permitted by the server. Usually, the IP address here refers to the client address seen from the server (such as the user’s gateway or proxy server address). In this case, the calculation of the number of connections may involve more than one end user.
422The request format is correct, but it cannot be responded to because it contains semantic errors. (RFC 4918 WebDAV) 423 Locked The current resource is locked. (RFC 4918 WebDAV)
424The current request failed due to an error in a previous request, for example PROPPATCH. (RFC 4918 WebDAV)
425Defined in the WebDav Advanced Collections draft, but not present in the WebDAV Ordered Collections Protocol (RFC 3658).
426The client should switch to TLS/1.0. (RFC 2817)
449A Microsoft extension, indicating that the request should be retried after appropriate operations have been performed.
500The server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from completing the processing of the request. Generally, this problem occurs when there is an error in the server’s program code.
501The server does not support a certain function required by the current request. When the server cannot recognize the request method and cannot support its requests for any resource.
502The server acting as a gateway or proxy received an invalid response from the upstream server while attempting to execute the request.
503Due to temporary server maintenance or overload, the server is currently unable to process the request. This situation is temporary and will recover after a period of time. If the delay time can be estimated, the response may contain a Retry-After header to indicate this delay time. If this Retry-After information is not given, the client should handle it in the same way as a 500 response. Note: The existence of the 503 status code does not mean that the server must use it when overloaded. Some servers simply wish to refuse client connections.
504The server acting as a gateway or proxy did not receive a timely response from the upstream server (the server identified by the URI, such as HTTP, FTP, LDAP) or an auxiliary server (such as DNS) while attempting to execute the request. Note: Some proxy servers return 400 or 500 errors when DNS queries time out.
505The server does not support, or refuses to support, the HTTP version used in the request. This implies that the server cannot or is unwilling to use the same version as the client. The response should contain an entity describing why the version is not supported and which protocols the server supports.
506Extended by the Transparent Content Negotiation Protocol (RFC 2295), indicating that the server has an internal configuration error: the requested negotiated variant resource is configured to use itself in transparent content negotiation, and therefore is not a suitable focus in a negotiation process.
507The server cannot store the content necessary to complete the request. This situation is considered temporary. WebDAV (RFC 4918)
509The server has reached its bandwidth limit. This is not an official status code, but it is still widely used.
510The policy required to obtain the resource has not been satisfied. (RFC 2774)

(This is part 1 of 2 of the same post.)

HTTP 状态码 - 维基百科

entry.content:
Preface

Note: all examples below use dummy proxies; replace them with your own.

Proxies are set for these situations:

  • Crossing the GFW Great Firewall, abbreviated as 翻墙
  • Accessing 外网 from 内网
  • Accessing 内网镜像库 from 内网 (npm, composer, etc.)

Proxy methods

There are at least the following ways to configure a proxy:

  • Set the target proxy machine (most common)

    e.g.: http://yourProxyServer:port

  • Set a PAC file to match proxies automatically (common in browsers)

    e.g.: http://example/a.pac

Proxy address

Assume your currently available proxy is: http://yourProxyServer:port; the examples below all use this proxy.

Windows CMD proxy settings

Effective for the current CMD window:

REM 设置代理set http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:portset https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:portREM 查看代理echo %http_proxy%echo %https_proxy%REM 取消代理(留空即可)set http_proxy=set https_proxy=

To make it permanent, set the system environment variables http_proxy and https_proxy, then restart Windows.

Notes:

  • http_proxy and https_proxy both correspond to http://yourProxyServer:port; the latter may not have the s of https.

Linux proxy settings

Same as the Mac proxy settings below ↓

Mac proxy settings

This section only covers configuring a proxy from the command line.

Add a shortcut for setting the proxy in ~/.bash_profile or ~/.zshrc:

# shadowsocks 翻墙用，不翻墙可不用alias proxy_ss='export all_proxy=socks5://127.0.0.1:1086; export http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:1087; export https_proxy=https://127.0.0.1:1087'# 其他代理alias proxy_dev='export http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port; export https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port'# 取消所有代理设置alias unproxy='unset all_proxy; unset http_proxy; unset https_proxy'

After setting it up, remember to source the config file.

To use it, run in the shell (using a dev machine as an example):

# 设置代理proxy_dev# 取消代理unproxy

Standalone commands:

# 临时设置代理export http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:portexport https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port# 查看代理echo $http_proxyecho $https_proxy# 取消代理unset http_proxyunset https_proxy

Mac Homebrew proxy settings

Same as the Mac command-line proxy settings above.

Brew 官方参考

Git proxy settings

Git

# 全局：设置 Git 访问外网（如 github）的代理git config --global http.proxy http://yourProxyServer:port# 全局：查看 Git 代理git config --global --get http.proxy# 全局：删除 Git 代理git config --global --unset http.proxy# ----------- 下面是针对每个项目局部的，非全局 -----------------# 设置 Git 访问外网（如 github）的代理git config http.proxy http://yourProxyServer:port# 查看 Git 代理git config --get http.proxy# 删除 Git 代理git config --unset http.proxy

Git username and email settings

# 设置 Git 全局：用户名、邮箱 ↓git config --global user.name "youName"git config --global user.email yourEmail@example.com# 下面是针对每个 Git 项目的，非全局 ↓git config user.email yourEmail@example.comgit config user.name "youName"

Which one to set globally and which one for the current project depends on your needs; there is no absolute rule.

npm proxy settings + registry settings

npm

Using the Taobao npm mirror (recommended)

In this case you need to set both: the Taobao mirror + your proxy (if any)

# ↓ 设置淘宝 npm 镜像npm config set registry https://registry.npmmirror.com# ↓ 若本来即可访问外网，无需下面代理设置npm config set https-proxy http://yourProxyServer:port

Using the official npm registry

Set the proxy (if any):

npm config set proxy http://yourProxyServer:portnpm config set https-proxy http://yourProxyServer:port

How to check npm proxy and registry settings

# 查看 npm 所有设置npm config list# 查看代理npm config get proxynpm config get https-proxy# 查看镜像npm config get registry# 取消代理npm config rm proxynpm config rm https-proxy

yarn proxy settings + registry settings

yarn

# 设置 registry 镜像yarn config set registry https://registry.npmmirror.com# 设置代理（若有的话）yarn config set proxy http://yourProxyServer:port# 查看所有设置yarn config list# 查看镜像设置yarn config get registry# 查看某个设置yarn config get proxy

yarn global config: 用户目录/.yarnrc

Notes:

  • Sometimes the proxy still doesn’t take effect; this may be caused by a problem with the yarn.lock file — try deleting it and starting over.

    • Reference: yarnpkg/yarn#4890

nvm proxy settings

nvm

# 设置代理（永久）nvm proxy "http://yourProxyServer:port"# 设置代理（临时，非必须）set http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:portset https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port# 查看代理nvm proxy# 删除代理nvm proxy "none"

Reference: https://github.com/coreybutler/nvm-windows#usage

Bower proxy settings

Bower

Create a new .bowerrc file and fill in proxy and https-proxy:

{  "directory": "bower_components",  "proxy": "http://yourProxyServer:port/",  "https-proxy": "http://yourProxyServer:port/"}

Three placement options are supported:

  • Current project: 当前目录（bower.json 的同级目录）
  • Current user’s home directory
  • System root directory (the / directory on Linux)

Reference: https://bower.io/docs/config/#placement--order

PHP Composer proxy settings

Composer

After installing Composer, Composer uses the system proxy directly (e.g., CMD on Windows); there is no proxy config file.

That is: on Windows you need to set the CMD proxy, something like

set http_proxy=yourProxyServer:portset https_proxy=yourProxyServer:port

Only then can you run composer require packageName

If the system has these two environment variables configured, that effectively acts as Composer’s global proxy.

PhpStorm, IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, Android Studio (or other JetBrains IDEs) proxy settings

Jetbrains

File -> Settings -> Appearance & Behavior -> System Settings

-> HTTP Proxy -> Manual proxy configuration -> HTTP

-> Host name: yourProxyServer -> Port number: yourProxyPort

-> OK

Maven proxy and mirror settings

Maven

Maven’s proxy and mirror settings are fairly extensive; see 这里 for details.

Gradle proxy settings

Gradle

  • To configure for the current project:
    • Create or edit gradle.properties inside the current project
  • To configure globally:
    • Create or edit 用户目录/.gradle/gradle.properties

Add the following settings to the gradle.properties file:

systemProp.http.proxyHost=yourProxyServersystemProp.http.proxyPort=yourPortsystemProp.https.proxyHost=yourProxyServersystemProp.https.proxyPort=yourPort

Reference: https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/build_environment.html

pip Proxy Settings for Python

pip is used to install Python packages.

There are 3 ways to set a proxy for pip (pick one):

  • System environment variables

    • Just like the CMD proxy settings, then pip install yourPackage, Win ↓
    set http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:portset https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port

  • --proxy parameter

    • pip install yourPackage --proxy http://yourProxyServer:port

  • pip.ini config file (recommended, permanent)

    • Taking Win as an example, create a new directory and file %HOME%\pip\pip.ini in your user directory, and fill in:

      [install]proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port

    • To check whether it worked: pip config list

Official pip documentation on setting a proxy: https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/user_guide/#using-a-proxy-server

VS Code Proxy Settings

VSCode reads the proxy from the http_proxy and https_proxy environment variables by default.

But you can also set it manually: File -> Preference -> Settings, then paste the following code into User Settings on the right:

"http.proxy": "http://yourProxyServer:port",

Notepad++ Proxy Settings

Notepad++

Menu bar -> question mark ? on the far right -> 设置更新代理服务器 ->

  • Proxy server: yourProxyServer
  • Port: yourPort

Sublime Proxy Settings

Sublime uses the system’s PAC settings by default. If your browser can get online, Sublime basically can too.

You can also customize the proxy in the config file:

  • 菜单栏 -> Preferences -> Settings -> 在左右任意一侧填入:
"http_proxy": "http://yourProxyServer:port","https_proxy": "http://yourProxyServer:port",

Eclipse Proxy Settings

Ways to set a proxy for Eclipse:

  • Window -> Preferences -> General -> Network Connections -> select Manual in Active Provider on the right -> double-click HTTP on line 1 under Proxy entries 表格 -> enter yourProxyServer in Host -> enter yourPort in Port -> OK
  • Set HTTPS and SOCKS the same way

Atom Editor Proxy Settings

Atom

See the commands below:

# 设置代理apm config set https-proxy https://yourProxyServer:port# 查看代理apm config get https-proxy# 查看所有配置（显示的结果的 `userconfig` 就是配置文件所在位置）apm config get

Reference: https://github.com/atom/apm#using-a-proxy

wget Proxy Settings

wget Win

wget Linux

Method 01 (temporary):

  • First set the proxy in Windows CMD:

    set http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:portset https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port

  • Or the proxy in a Linux shell:

    export http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:portexport https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port

  • Then you can use the wget command directly

Method 02 (permanent, recommended!):

  • Just use the wget config file: create a new file .wgetrc in the current user’s home directory (or /etc/wgetrc on Linux):

    http-proxy = yourProxyServer:porthttps-proxy = yourProxyServer:portftp-proxy = yourProxyServer:port

  • Then you can use the wget command directly

Method 03 (temporary):

  • Add parameters directly to the wget command, e.g.
    • wget https://www.baidu.com -e https-proxy=yourProxyServer:port
    • or (both are http, not https)
    • wget http://www.baidu.com -e http-proxy=yourProxyServer:port

curl Proxy Settings

curl

Method 01 (temporary):
(This is part 2 of 4 of the same post.)

  • First, set the proxy for Windows CMD:
    set http_proxy=yourProxyServer:portset https_proxy=yourProxyServer:port
  • Or the proxy for the Linux shell:
    export http_proxy=yourProxyServer:portexport https_proxy=yourProxyServer:port
  • Then you can use the curl command directly, for example
    • curl http://www.baidu.com -o baidu.html

Method 02 (permanent, recommended!):

  • Just use the curl config file. Create a new config file in the current user’s home directory (Win: _curlrc) (Linux: .curlrc):
    proxy = yourProxyServer:port
  • Then you can use the curl command directly, for example
    • curl http://www.baidu.com -o baidu.html

Method 03 (temporary):

  • Add the parameter directly to the curl command, for example
    • curl https://www.baidu.com -o baidu.html -x yourProxyServer:port

      -x The lowercase x means proxy

Golang’s go get Proxy

Golang’s go get uses the system’s http_proxy, but pulling code uses Git’s proxy,
so you need to do both steps:

  1. Set the system proxy (or CMD proxy)
set http_proxy=yourProxyServer:port
  1. Set the Git proxy, see Git 代理设置 above
git config --global http.proxy http://yourProxyServer:port

References:

  • https://stackoverflow.com/a/10385612/2752670
  • Official reference: https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/GoGetProxyConfig

If you use VS Code, and want VS Code to automatically download Go’s dependency tools, you should also set the proxy in VS Code’s settings.json:

"http.proxy": "http://yourProxyServer:port",

Navicat Connecting to an External Database

Navicat seemingly requires configuring both 通道地址 and 代理服务器.

Note: This method is not very secure; use it with caution!

  • Step 01: In the Navicat installation directory, find the file: C:\Program Files\PremiumSoft\Navicat Premium\ntunnel_mysql.php (or the php for the corresponding language), and place it in your external web service directory (open http://IP:port/abc/ntunnel_mysql.php in a browser and you should see a page)
  • Step 02: 右键某个数据库连接 -> HTTP -> check 使用 HTTP 通道 -> fill in http://IP:port/abc/ntunnel_mysql.php for 通道地址 -> below 代理服务器 -> check 使用代理服务器 -> fill in yourPorxyServer for 主机 -> fill in yourPort for 端口 -> 测试连接 -> 确定

VirtualBox and VMware Proxy Settings

Most users run their VMs in NAT mode.

Proxy settings: the system inside the VM must use the same proxy settings as the host physical machine in order to get online.

Xshell Proxy Settings

Open the properties of a session

  • Connection
  • Proxy
  • Browse
  • Add
    • Name: anyName (or any name you like)
    • Type: HTTP 1.1
    • Host: yourProxyServer
    • Port: yourPort
    • OK
    • Close
  • For Proxy Server, select the proxy you just created
  • Done

SecureCRT Proxy Settings

Two steps: first add a global proxy entry, then select the corresponding proxy entry in each connection.

  1. Add a global proxy entry
  • Options
  • Global Options
  • Firewall
    • Add
      • Name: anyName (or any name you like)
      • Type: HTTP (no authentication)
      • Hostname or IP: yourProxyServer
      • Port: yourPort
      • OK
  1. Select the newly created proxy entry in your connection
  • Your connection -> Properties
  • Connection
  • SSH2
  • Firewall
  • Select 刚新建的代理项

Proxifier: Setting Up a Proxy for Other Software

Proxifier

Unlike the previous software, where each sets its own proxy, Proxifier takes a different approach: it sets up a proxy for other software uniformly.

Advantages:

  • No need to configure proxies separately for each app in its own way
  • Apps without a proxy settings UI work well with Proxifier
  • You can see the actual traffic of the proxied apps
  • Works on both Windows and Mac

Drawbacks:

  • Proxy settings aren’t always granular enough (e.g., Git’s global proxy vs. the proxy for the current Git project)

Steps:

  1. 菜单栏 Profile -> Proxy Servers -> Add -> Address, enter yourProxyServer -> Port, enter yourPort -> Protocol, enter HTTPS -> OK
  2. 菜单栏 Profile -> Proxification Rules -> Add -> Name, fill in anything - > Applications select the exe file of the app you want to proxy via the Browse button -> Action choose the yourProxyServer set in the previous steps -> OK

Credits

Thanks to Dylan for the proxy roundup!

This article is reposted from: dylan-7/note/blob/main/常用代理设置汇总.md

entry.content:
• This tutorial uses the xizeyoupan/Meting-API open-source project on GitHub to deploy your own serverless Meting-API
  • This article is mainly aimed at those without a server; if you have one, you can switch to this repository metowolf/Meting-API for deployment
  • Benefits of self-hosting: no one else controls your API calls, and there’s no risk of the service shutting down, because the API is in your own hands
  • Demo Test: meting-api.saop.cc/test

Prerequisites

  1. Register a GitHub account (skip this if you already have one)
  2. Register a Vercel account (skip this if you already have one)
  3. Have a tool that can access the GitHub and Vercel websites (a VPN)
  4. A domain of your own and some basic computer knowledge
  5. A pair of hands, a brain, a pair of eyes, and a computer or phone

Tutorial

0x0001

Go to the repository of the xizeyoupan/Meting-API open-source project, click the Fork button in the top right corner to fork the main branch of this repository,

Go to the Vercel platform and click Add New... > Project, use your brain a little, and add the repository you just forked,

0x0002

After the deployment succeeds, go to the project’s Settings > Domains custom domains, add your own subdomain, like mine meting-api.saop.cc

Go to your domain’s DNS provider (for example, Tencent Cloud for my domain) and add the CNAME record provided by Vercel

0x0003

Wait a bit, about two or three minutes, then visit the domain you just bound 二级域名/test, for example https://meting-api.saop.cc/test

If you get an error, start over from the beginning; it’s usually a mistake in your own operations. If it succeeds, the following test page will appear:

The top left of each song shows the provider and the retrieved type, corresponding to:

Original nameProviderType
tencent playlistQQ MusicPlaylist
tencent songQQ MusicTrack
netease playlistNetEase Cloud MusicPlaylist
netease songNetEase Cloud MusicTrack
netease artistNetEase Cloud MusicArtist
ytmusic playlistYouTubePlaylist
ytmusic songYouTubeTrack
spotify playlistSpotifyPlaylist
spotify songSpotifyTrack

If some provider or type is blank, it means data can’t be retrieved for that provider or type, so avoid that option when using it

Usage

API Parameters

  • server: data source

    • netease: NetEase Cloud Music
    • tencent: QQ Music

  • type: type

    • name: song name
    • artist: artist
    • url: link
    • pic: cover
    • lrc: lyrics
    • song: track
    • playlist: playlist

  • id: the ID for the type (cover ID / track ID / playlist ID)

  • For example:

    • https://meting-api.saop.cc/api?server=netease&type=url&id=416892104
    • https://meting-api.saop.cc/api?server=netease&type=song&id=591321
    • https://meting-api.saop.cc/api?server=netease&type=playlist&id=2619366284

Embedding the API in Meting.min.js

Save the Meting.min.js file to your own device

Meting.min.js: https://npm.elemecdn.com/meting/dist/Meting.min.js

Edit this file, press Ctrl + F to search for api?server=, replace https://api.i-meto.com/meting/api?server= with your own API, then press Ctrl + S to save

  • Before: https://api.i-meto.com/meting/api?server=
  • After: https://meting-api.saop.cc/api?server=

Once you’ve replaced it, you can put it in your code space and reference this file via a link, or place it locally and reference it with a relative link

Applying to the Butterfly theme for Hexo

Make sure the APlayer music plugin is enabled before configuring, otherwise the configuration won’t do anything…

Place the Meting.min.js file into the [站点根目录]\source\js folder and edit the theme configuration file _config.butterfly.yml,

Change the CDN link of the meting_js: option to /js/Meting.min.js

# CDN# Don't modify the following settings unless you know how they work# 非必要請不要修改CDN:  # The CDN provider of internal scripts (主題內部 js 的 cdn 配置)  # option: local/jsdelivr/unpkg/cdnjs/custom  # Dev version can only choose. ( dev版的主題只能設置為 local )  internal_provider: local  # The CDN provider of third party scripts (第三方 js 的 cdn 配置)  # option: local/jsdelivr/unpkg/cdnjs/custom  # when set it to local, you need to install hexo-butterfly-extjs  third_party_provider: unpkg  # Add version number to CDN, true or false  version: false  # Custom format  # For example: https://cdn.staticfile.org/${cdnjs_name}/${version}/${min_cdnjs_file}  custom_format:  option:    aplayer_css: https://npm.elemecdn.com/aplayer/dist/APlayer.min.css    aplayer_js: https://npm.elemecdn.com/aplayer/dist/APlayer.min.js    meting_js: /js/Meting.min.js

Finally, the usual Hexo three-step combo, of course!

hexo cl; hexo g; hexo s

You can press F12 to check whether the Meting.min.js file has loaded

Credits

GitHub: xizeyoupan/Meting-API
